transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~57 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Rachel (Redwood PM), Diego (Redwood Solutions); Mark, Jules, Anya, Samir (Mariner)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to validate marketplace listing networking patterns, on-prem/edge connectivity flows, KMS and telemetry contract; run a short lab to reproduce connection handoffs and confirm observability events for billing and SLAs.

Topics:
- VPC peering vs PrivateLink style connector for Mariner edge gateways
- KMS/HSM key flow for onprem private deployments and marketplace listing requirements
- Telemetry event schema + span correlation for token-level cost traces
- Packaging: Helm chart overlays, image registry creds, and canary routing hooks
- Lab plan and immediate next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. We wanted to keep this focused on connectivity and the telemetry contract for listing Mariner on the marketplace. Priya will lead the lab bits.
[00:22] Mark (Mariner): Thanks, Alex. We have Samir and Anya on the call from infra and security, and Jules from product. We're mainly worried about how the Redwood connector will operate from our edge gateways where we do low-latency inference.
[00:38] Priya (SE): Cool. Quick question - are you planning to use the hosted Redwood API for routing, or do you want the Private deployment with our control-plane in your VPC? I know you mentioned a hybrid earlier.
[00:50] Jules (Product): Hybrid, yes. We want to run inference near our customers but still have a marketplace managed listing so easier upgrades. So Private control-plane + local runtime is the target.
[01:05] Rachel (PM): We'll need the listing to support both "private" and a dedicated-reserved capacity option so customers can opt for hosted fallback. That's why routing and graceful fallback matter.
[01:20] Samir (SRE): From a networking perspective we prefer a connector pattern - short-lived mutual TLS over an outbound-only connection - rather than inbound peering. We can't accept peering.
[01:37] Priya: That maps well to Redwood's agent model. We have an outbound TLS tunnel pattern for private deployments that talks back to the control plane via a connector layer. The marketplace packaging expects a helm chart with a connector sidecar.
[01:52] Mark: Sidecar is fine, but we need to validate metrics and logs, can we get structured telemetry out of that sidecar? Our billing team needs per-request token accounting.
[02:08] Diego (Solutions): We already have lightweight span headers and per-token counters in the runtime. The question is the format you need - like OTLP, JSON lines, or a CSV dump?
[02:20] Mark: OTLP preferred, we use Jaeger/Tempo internally, but we also ingest JSON logs into our ELK for quick queries.
[02:33] Priya: We can emit OTLP traces and JSON events; will need to confirm what headers you want for token attribution. Typically we emit request_id, model, seq_len, token_count, and cost_usd_estimate fields.
[02:50] Anya (Security): On encryption - we need the key material to be customer-managed. If it's marketplace listing we need an option to bring-your-own KMS key and HSM integration for the private runtime.
[03:05] Alex: Yep, BYOK is supported. For Private we integrate with customer KMS via an ARN you provide; there is an HSM path for FIPS use cases but that adds packaging complexity.
[03:20] Jules: Packaging complexity = time to certify. What's the delta on our side if we opt for HSM?
[03:30] Priya: Mainly the installer will require the HSM client and a slightly different secrets flow. It also affects how we rotate keys; the marketplace listing docs include an HSM checklist. We'll share that.
[03:45] Mark: Ok. For connectivity lab, we want to reproduce a connection flapping scenario and observe fallback to hosted variant; also validate metrics emitted during the failover.
[04:00] Priya: Good. My plan is a two-phase lab: 1) connectivity tunnel bring-up in a test VPC with the helm overlay and sidecar, 2) induce degraded conditions (simulate packet loss, short SG drop) and watch routing for canary fallback. I'll need a small VM or a k8s test cluster in your environment to run this.
[04:20] Samir: We can spin up a short-lived k8s cluster in our dev project and give a service account. We'll also whitelist Redwood control-plane IPs.
[04:33] Alex: Please make sure the whitelist is for outbound only; we shouldn't need inbound peering.
[04:40] Anya: We'll also want to test key rotation in the lab. If the private runtime loses KMS access mid-flight, how do you handle cached keys?
[04:55] Priya: The runtime caches encryption keys but never the raw plaintext; on KMS failure we will fail safe and optionally degrade to a cached tokenizer path. Behavior configurable - default is to return errors for calls requiring encryption. We'll show logs during the lab.
[05:14] Jules: About marketplace listing metadata, we need a sample Helm values override to inject our registry creds and network settings. Can you share an example?
[05:30] Alex: Yes - I'll push a values.yaml example with overrides for outbound proxy, custom registry, and KMS ARNs. Also include the canary routing toggles.
[05:43] Mark: One thing we ran into with other vendors: metric cardinality explodes when token-level events are emitted for every request. We need aggregation options.
[05:58] Diego: We support per-call sampling and aggregation. In the sidecar you can enable prefix-aggregation (by model+customer) and only send full token traces for sampled requests. That reduces cardinality but preserves observability.
[06:16] Samir: That sampling approach sounds reasonable. What about correlating token counts with billing? If sampled we might undercount.
[06:30] Priya: We send an estimated token_count field for every request even if the full trace isn't emitted. So billing can use these counts; full traces are for debugging.
[06:44] Anya: Security compliance: we need audit logs for admin actions and listing updates. Does Redwood provide authenticated change logs that we can pull into our SIEM?
[06:58] Alex: Yes, there is an audit API. For Private listing we can forward audit events to your S3 or push via Kinesis; we'll provide a connector pattern.
[07:12] Mark: Good. For the lab, we will provide a redacted S3 bucket to receive audit events.
[07:21] Priya: Great. Next, packaging - some of our edge customers run air-gapped deployments. How does the marketplace install handle air-gap?
[07:36] Diego: We produce an air-gap tarball with images and a manifest. The helm chart supports --set imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent and an offline registry config. We do recommend signing images for supply-chain assurance.
[07:51] Jules: Do you support sigstore or cosign signatures?
[07:58] Priya: Cosign is supported in our CI pipeline; we'll provide signed manifests on request for your air-gap bundles.
[08:10] Samir: On upgrade, air-gap is tricky. Can we do in-place upgrades with canary rollout on an air-gapped cluster?
[08:22] Diego: Yes, provided you mirror the new tarball into your registry and update the helm values. Canary routing is a runtime feature so it works offline. We'll show the helm hooks in the lab.
[08:37] Mark: Telemetry schema - Samir will need a sample of events to validate ingestion.
[08:45] Priya: I'll attach a small JSON lines sample after the call. It will include fields: request_id, trace_id, model_name, seq_len, token_count, estimated_cost_usd, runtime_ms, node_id, cluster_tag.
[09:02] Mark: Perfect. Also include an example of OTLP span attributes so we can correlate traces to logs.
[09:10] Diego: We'll ensure the span has the same trace_id and request_id.
[09:15] Anya: For SOC2 evidence, we may need the exact retention settings for telemetry retained in Redwood control plane vs what stays on-prem.
[09:26] Alex: Control plane telemetry aggregation is configurable; by default we retain 90 days in the hosted analytics and you can configure retention for private deploys. We'll include the retention table in the security packet.
[09:40] Jules: About the marketplace listing metadata: is there a mandatory set of docs or do we provide a short description + install guide?
[09:49] Alex: Mandatory: listing description, architecture diagram, reference values.yaml, and a compliance checklist. Optional: bench results and latency/cost profiles. We'll provide a template.
[10:02] Mark: Benchmarking: we want to run a 10-minute throughput test that mimics our 10k QPS edge bursts. Can Redwood run that from dedicated?
[10:16] Priya: We can schedule an hour on a dedicated pool for benchmarking. But for accurate edge latency numbers we prefer you run the load generator in your dev cluster and stream metrics to us. We can help with the runner.
[10:31] Samir: Ok we'll provision the load runner. We'll also want to verify model variant fallback - when the local runtime is saturated it should route to a smaller quantized variant hosted in the cloud.
[10:46] Diego: That's supported via smart routing. You can configure fallback policies: latency-first or cost-first. We'll demo policy evaluation in the lab.
[10:57] Mark: One operational concern - how do we handle tenant isolation and per-customer quotas? Our customers expect per-tenant rate limiting.
[11:10] Priya: Runtime supports per-tenant tokens and per-route quotas enforced at the edge. The marketplace listing will need to expose quota knobs in the values.yaml.
[11:21] Jules: For the listing, is there a way to include our SLA text and have the marketplace display it?
[11:30] Alex: Yes, there's a field in the listing metadata for SLA bullet points; legal will need to sign the marketplace contract and we'll surface the SLA there.
[11:39] Anya: A quick question on secrets: do you mount secrets as files or inject via env? We prefer secrets mounted and never in process env.
[11:49] Priya: We support both, but the helm chart defaults to kubernetes secrets volume mount for key material. We'll show the values to choose mounts.
[11:59] Mark: Great. For the lab, we'll need the helm chart and an example manifest with our registry + KMS ARNs.
[12:08] Alex: I'll share a repo link after the call.
[12:14] Priya: Now small demo walkthrough - I'll share my screen and show the connector bring up. (screen share noise)
[12:30] [screen share noises, brief pause]
[12:45] Priya: Ok, here's the helm release. Notice the connector config under values.connectivity.connector_url and the sidecar image. I'm toggling sampling.rate=0.01 to show how we reduce payload.
[13:05] Mark: That value looks good. Can we tie sampling to a header so we can force full traces for specific customer requests?
[13:18] Priya: Yes, header-driven sampling is supported: X-Rw-ForceTrace=1 will force a full trace for that request_id.
[13:29] Samir: We'll need to ensure that doesn't leak PII. Is the full trace scrubbed?
[13:36] Diego: We redact PII by default; we also support field-level redaction rules that you can set in values.yaml.
[13:49] Anya: Another compliance ask: can we opt out of storing embeddings in the control plane? We want some customers to keep embeddings on-prem.
[13:59] Priya: Embeddings can be configured to store locally; the control plane can keep pointer metadata only. We'll include that configuration in the listing doc.
[14:12] Jules: Good. A blocker we had with another provider was channel-based authentication - they required static credentials for the sidecar. We want short-lived certs.
[14:24] Priya: We use short-lived cert rotation via a mTLS bootstrap. The connector does a signed CSR against your KMS/HSM-backed CA if you provide one; otherwise our control plane vends short certs.
[14:38] Mark: Ok that meets our security bar.
[14:44] Diego: For the lab plan I'll outline steps: install helm chart, configure registry and KMS, start connector, send 1k QPS burst, induce flapping by blocking egress to control-plane IPs for 30s, observe fallback. We also capture OTLP streams to your collector.
[15:04] Samir: We'll provide a dev cluster and an S3 bucket for audit logs. We'll also provide a pre-provisioned KMS key ARN for testing (in a dev account).
[15:15] Alex: Excellent. Timeline wise, if the lab goes well we can run a small pilot with 2 customers in Dec and aim to publish the listing in Jan.
[15:30] Jules: Jan publish sounds ambitious but ok if packaging and compliance checkboxes are green.
[15:39] Anya: For the compliance packet please include: SOC2 scoping, retention tables, KMS integration doc, and signed image attestations.
[15:52] Alex: We'll assemble the packet and send the link to the shared drive.
[16:00] Priya: Quick note on cost telemetry - estimated_cost_usd is an estimate using token pricing; for accurate billing you'll need to map those events back to your billing pipeline. We'll share a mapping doc.
[16:15] Mark: That will be helpful.
[16:20] Diego: One more operational note: when you list, you can enable an "upgrade window" which delays auto-upgrades for N days so customers can test. We recommend 7 days.
[16:32] Jules: We'll likely use 14 days for edge customers.
[16:37] Priya: Noted. Now let's capture explicit next steps and owners.
[16:45] Alex: Recap: Priya runs the connectivity lab (we'll tentatively schedule for Nov 23). Alex shares listing checklist and helm example today. Mariner to share telemetry sample and KMS ARN by Nov 25. Anya to confirm SOC2 contact by Nov 24.
[17:05] Mark: Sounds good. Anything else?
[17:10] Samir: One last: can Redwood share a short runbook for fallback troubleshooting? A 1-page playbook we can paste into our runbooks.
[17:20] Diego: We'll produce a 1-page runbook as part of the lab artifacts.
[17:27] Alex: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the repo links.
[17:37] Jules: Thanks all.
[17:40] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions and minor word errors may be present; original audio had a brief screen-share silence at ~12:30.
